sample_unit: patients with primary knee osteoarthritis completing 6-month follow-up

links.outcome: LLM 6-month outcome prediction error versus physician predictions and a persistence model
links.effect: LLM WOMAC MAE 5.92-6.58 vs physician 3.86 and persistence model 5.43; KL exact agreement 66.7%-68.5% vs physician 86.5%. LLM worse than physician and not superior to persistence model.
links.quote: The LLM showed high baseline diagnostic agreement with the physician (105/111, 94.6%) and good agreement on the WOMAC and KL, but 6-month predictions (WOMAC mean absolute error=5.92-6.58; KL exact agreement=74/111, 66.7%-76/111, 68.5%) were worse than those of the physician comparator (mean absolute error=3.86; 96/111, 86.5%) and not superior to those of the persistence model (mean absolute error=5.43).

links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM outputs across 3 independent runs
links.effect: Interrun ICCs were high (0.982 and 0.965), but exact agreement between runs was poor (35/111, 31.5% and 7/111, 6.3%).
links.quote: Despite high interrun intraclass correlation coefficients (0.982 and 0.965), exact agreement between runs was poor (35/111, 31.5% and 7/111, 6.3%).

screen.reason: Evaluates the accuracy and reproducibility of an LLM (DeepSeek) in predicting clinical/radiographic outcomes from patient records compared to a physician and a persistence model; it does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
